name: Belgium
summary: 1921 drug law with generic bans on whole NPS groups (2017). Adults with ≤3 g cannabis or one plant usually only get a simplified police report, but it stays illegal. Recreational nitrous banned since 2024.
callingForHelp: Ambulance (112) staff are bound by professional secrecy and police are not routinely called for an overdose. No specific Good Samaritan protection.
drugChecking: Available in Brussels through Modus Vivendi's testing service; very limited elsewhere.

lsd.note: Possession, purchase and sale are banned; use is punished via possession. Penalties: 3 months–5 years and/or fines.

mushrooms.note: Hallucinogenic mushrooms and magic truffles (Psilocybe etc.) are illegal in any amount, despite Dutch smartshop claims.

dmt.note: DMT is banned; possession, sale and use of ayahuasca are illegal.

mescaline.note: Mescaline and peyote cactus are banned; the status of San Pedro cactus was not verified.

dox.note: DOB and related amphetamines are banned, individually and through the 2017 generic amphetamine group ban.

nbomes.note: 25B-, 25C- and 25I-NBOMe are internationally controlled; other NBOMes are likely covered by the 2017 generic group bans.

2c-x.note: 2C-B has been banned since 1998; other 2C-x fall under the 2017 generic group bans.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are internationally controlled; other 2C-T-x are likely covered by the 2017 generic group bans.

5-meo-xxt.note: Tryptamines are banned as a group since the 2017 royal decree, covering 5-MeO-DMT, 5-MeO-MiPT and similar.

cannabis.note: Adults with ≤3 g or one female plant usually get a simplified police report and seizure (lowest priority). Minors, nuisance or minors present: prosecution.

ketamine.note: Controlled under narcotics law; legal only on prescription (hospital/vet use). Illegal possession: 3 months–5 years and/or fines.

mxe.note: Controlled (EU-wide since 2014) and covered by the 2017 generic bans.

dxm.note: Licensed cough medicine sold in pharmacies; not a controlled drug. Whether a prescription is needed was not verified.

nitrous.note: Since 8 Apr 2024, buying, possessing or using it recreationally is an offence (fine €120–200 for a first offence); sale to minors banned since 2021.

amphetamines.note: Speed and methamphetamine are banned; possession can bring 3 months–5 years and/or fines. Doctors may prescribe amphetamines in some cases.

mdma.note: Banned; possession can bring 3 months–5 years prison and/or fines.

cocaine.note: Banned; possession can bring 3 months–5 years prison and/or fines; trafficking much more.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Beer and wine from 16; spirits and spirit-based drinks from 18. Vending machines need ID-card age checks.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB banned since 1996; GBL also controlled since the 2017 royal decree. Status of 1,4-BD not verified.

opioids.note: Heroin is banned (possession: 3 months–5 years and/or fines). Morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl etc. only on prescription.

benzodiazepines.note: Sold only on prescription in pharmacies; controlled psychotropic medicines.

maois.note: Pharmaceutical MAOIs are prescription-only. Ayahuasca is illegal (DMT); harmala/Syrian rue status not verified.
